name: Male Lower Urinary Tract, Prostate and Testicular Anatomy

reference.source: ALGrawany Anatomy & Physiology Made Easy 2026 / Campbell-Walsh Urology
clinicalPearls: Ureter has 3 physiological constrictions: pelviureteric junction, pelvic brim crossing, and intramural bladder wall
Detrusor muscle is innervated by parasympathetics (S2-S4); bladder trigone is derived from mesoderm
Prostate peripheral zone accounts for 75% of carcinomas; transition zone is the site of benign prostatic hyperplasia
Testicular lymph drains to para-aortic (lumbar) nodes; scrotal skin drains to superficial inguinal nodes
Torsion of spermatic cord cuts off venous and arterial blood supply, requiring surgical detorsion within 6 hours
reference.pathophysiology: Ureteral smooth muscle propels urine into the bladder via peristaltic contractions. Calculi commonly impact at narrow anatomical bottlenecks. The prostate surrounds the bladder neck; nodular hyperplasia of the transition zone compresses the prostatic urethra, causing lower urinary tract symptoms, while carcinomas arise mainly in the peripheral zone.
additionalInvestigations: Non-contrast CT kidneys, ureters, bladder (CT KUB) for nephrolithiasis
Serum prostate-specific antigen (PSA) and multi-parametric prostate MRI (PI-RADS)
Scrotal Doppler ultrasound for acute testicular pain and torsion
